summary: Add a visual trend model and targeted retrieval practice for electronegativity factors, while clarifying its distinction from first ionisation energy.

improvements.where: note, after the across-period paragraph in ## Key ideas
improvements.why: Outcome 9701-3.1.3 asks learners to state and explain the across-period trend, and several past-paper items ask them to recognise it from a graph; the chapter has no diagram.
improvements.what: Use graph_sketch to show the general rise in Pauling electronegativity from Na to Cl across Period 3, with element labels and an annotation that increasing nuclear charge and decreasing radius strengthen attraction. Keep the plotted line schematic rather than implying exact values; embed it in the note and explain what to notice.

improvements.where: note, after the trend paragraphs in ## Key ideas
improvements.why: Past-paper graph comparisons with first ionisation energy can prompt learners to copy its Mg–Al or P–S dips into electronegativity; the current warning in Exam technique gives no reason.
improvements.what: Add a brief side-by-side explanation: electronegativity concerns attraction in a bond and generally rises across Period 3; first ionisation energy concerns removing a gaseous atom's electron and can show subshell and paired-electron dips. State that those dips must not be transferred mechanically to an electronegativity sketch.

improvements.why: The only flashcard checks the definition, leaving the three causal factors and both trend explanations without spaced retrieval.
improvements.what: Add concise flashcards asking for the three factors, why electronegativity rises across a period, and why it falls down a group; backs should link nuclear charge, radius and shielding to electron attraction.

improvements.why: Existing structured questions test trend statements and explanations, while the graph-reading practice is only in extra MCQs; a learner should articulate why a tempting first-ionisation-energy-shaped graph is wrong.
improvements.what: Add an exam-style short item showing or describing a Period 3 graph with a false Mg–Al or P–S dip; ask the learner to identify the incorrect feature and explain the general electronegativity trend using nuclear charge, radius and shielding.
